text:
maya: Seeing intermittent throughput drops on L40S when FP8 kernels pick \"tiling_v2\". Happens ~every 10-20s for long-chat traces. Throughput dips ~30% for a few tokens then recovers. Anyone seen thermal/stutter-like patterns with FP8 on L40S?

sam: Noticed something similar on a 128k token replay earlier this week. Do you have a perf trace or kernel selection log?

maya: Pasting the lightweight profiler snippet (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] kernel_select: tiling_v2 (FP8) chosen for layer 12
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] kv_cache: hit_ratio=0.92, active_entries=32768
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] gpu_metrics: util=98%, temp=72C, power=310W
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] latency: token=18ms (baseline 12ms)
[2026-03-10T14:21:12Z] fallback: switched to safe_accel int8_path for 2 tokens
```

maya: Note: temp is stable, so not a thermal throttle. The switch seems tied to a microbatch shape change (sometimes microbatch=1 -> 4).

eli: Two quick hypotheses: kernel tiling mismatch on small microbatches causes memory stride pathological case; and transformer-engine JIT selects a different actuator when FP8 quant params cross a threshold. We had an internal bug where FP8 scale clipping triggered a different kernel selector.

toni: Also check KV layout serialization. If the runtime re-packs KV cache between kernel variants the memcpy cost + small batch amplifies the latency blip. We saw this with the new microbatch packing heuristic.

sam: Can you try forcing the kernel selector to stable tiling_v1 for a quick repro? Add this to runtime config and rerun: 

```json
{"quant": {"enable_fp8": true, "fp8_policy": "aggressive"}, "kernel_selector": {"preferred": ["tiling_v1"], "force_on_mismatch": true}, "microbatch_packing": {"max_pack": 4, "min_pack": 2}}
```

maya: Tried forcing tiling_v1 — stutter gone in the short run but overall throughput dropped 6% (so tiling_v2 is faster overall when stable). Means tiling_v2 has a narrow stability window.

eli: That's telling — we should add a guard in the selector that avoids tiling_v2 when microbatch variance > 0.3 or when KV repack rate > X/s.

perf-ci: perf alert: regression detected on master vs canary. Median p50 token latency +18%. Stack: kernel_selection -> kv_repack -> small_microbatch penalty.

maya: Also observed model-quality noise (a handful of tokens got slight FP8 saturation leading to occasional sampling changes). Could be calibration drift under batch shape churn.

toni: For next steps: 1) Add a telemetry gate for kernel transitions (emit event with old/new kernel + microbatch_size + kv_repack flag). 2) Add a transient backoff: after a kernel switch, pin kernel for N tokens unless memory pressure forces switch. 3) Re-evaluate transformer-engine flags (TF_ENGINE_JIT_LEVEL / TF_ENGINE_FORCE_NVFUSER) since they change kernel variant inference.

eli: Small config to try (dev-only):

```bash
export TF_ENGINE_FORCE_NVFUSER=1
# runtime flag to reduce selector chatter
--selector-stability-threshold=0.25
--fp8-scale-clamp=0.98
```

maya: I'll run a 3-hour replay with telemetry gates and pinned kernel backoff. Posting logs in this thread once done.

sam: If you get repro, open ops ticket and cc eng-infra + eng-ml. Might need a microbatch packing rollback or a selector tweak.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-10T15:00 -> rolled back after latency spike detected :warning:

maya: Result from 3-hour run (short summary): stutter frequency dropped by ~85% with pin-backoff + selector-threshold=0.25. P50 improved vs canary but p99 still has rare spikes linked to KV repack during long-context divergence.

toni: Good progress. I'll file an RFC for a more deterministic KV layout across kernel variants and propose a small change to microbatch packing to prefer uniform shapes.

eli: I'll push a prototype selector patch that uses a tiny online model to predict microbatch-cost delta and avoid tiling_v2 when predicted penalty > 2ms.

maya: Assigning follow-ups: @toni - KV layout RFC; @eli - selector patch PR; @sam - ops ticket + rollback plan if canary regresses.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
